title: Bridge room diary — incident rotation (2026-06-18)
content:
Purpose: short-form bridge-room notes from the on-call rotation on 2026-06-18. This is a working log intended for handoff, follow-up triage, and quick-runbook updates. Not a final postmortem.

Quick summary:
- Two customer-visible incidents during the shift: a partial degradation of hosted inference latency (INC-2387) and an embedding pipeline retry storm that increased queue lengths for ~45m.
- No user data exposure. No SLA credit requests expected at this time; error budget burn limited but visible for p99 latency on the hosted-api route.
- Immediate mitigations restored service; follow-ups assigned for deep-dive and monitoring hardening.

Incident A — hosted-api p99 latency spike (INC-2387):
- Detect: 2026-06-18 03:12 UTC — p99 latency for /v1/generate jumped from baseline ~200ms to 1.2s. Alert: latency_p99_shipping_rule fired.
- Scope: ~6% of requests, concentrated in region-us-west1 and primarily small-sequence chat requests.
- Initial hypothesis: degraded KV cache hit-rate after a model variant rollout combined with a pathological request shape (many small prompts causing inefficient batching).
- Mitigation timeline:
  - 03:14 UTC: On-call (Ava) routed new requests to fallback model-variant (gptx-lite-1) via runtime-routing override; immediate p99 improvement to ~280ms.
  - 03:20 UTC: Increased batch flush timeout from 12ms -> 6ms for the affected pool to favor latency over efficiency (temporary).
  - 03:28 UTC: Cache warming job kicked off for full prefix set; hit-rate recovered over 18 minutes.
- Root-cause (work-in-progress): rollout of quantized variant (qv2) changed tokenization boundary behavior for some prompt templates, reducing cache reuse. Secondary factor: recent kernel upgrade introduced a slightly higher collectives latency under partial load.
- Actions and owners:
  - Marcus Li: rollback or pin qv2 for us-west1 until quantization tokenization fix is validated (owner, actioned 2026-06-18 04:00 UTC)
  - Sofia Gomez: add synthetic load tests covering small-sequence chat patterns and measure batching behavior (owner, due 2026-06-25)
  - Create a targeted eval to detect tokenization boundary changes in new model variants (linked JIRA-RWF-2391).

Incident B — embedding pipeline retry storm: 
- Detect: 2026-06-18 07:04 UTC — embedding-queue lag increased; multiple workers started retrying with exponential backoff leading to backlog.
- Scope: internal batch ingestion (nearline) only; customer-facing embedding endpoints not directly impacted but downstream jobs slowed.
- Cause: transitive Kafka consumer group rebalance after a broker maintenance; consumers retried and hit a bug in the backoff logic that retriggered duplicate retries for the same message id.
- Mitigation:
  - 07:08 UTC: throttled ingestion traffic at edge (rate-limit flag) to let backlog drain.
  - 07:21 UTC: patched consumer library to skip duplicate retries for known message ids (hotfix PR: infra#412).
  - 07:35 UTC: broker partition placement adjusted to avoid hot-spots.
- Follow-ups:
  - Jordan Reed: clean up retry-idempotency logic and add unit tests (owner, due 2026-06-30).
  - Add an alert for consumer-group rebalance frequency > 3 in 10m (owner: SRE monitoring team, due 2026-06-22).

SLO snapshot (observed during shift):
- hosted-api availability (5xx < 0.1% monthly target): 99.985% (within target this window).
- hosted-api latency SLO (p99 < 400ms): rolling 7d shows 0.6% violations; today spike pushed instantaneous p99 to 1.2s for ~16 minutes. Current monthly projection: minor burn but still under error budget.
- embedding pipeline throughput SLO: briefly reduced to 68% of committed throughput during backlog, normalized after 08:10 UTC.

Monitoring & dashboards notes:
- Observed that the p99 alert threshold was tuned to 1.0s; consider lowering to 800ms for early warning on similar pathological cases (proposal in JIRA-RWF-2395).
- KV cache metrics are not surfaced at the per-model-variant level — makes triage slower. Tagging: observability owners to add model_variant dimension to cache_hit_rate metric (Sofia).

Runbook edits (quick wins):
- Add a one-click runtime-routing toggle to pin requests to a stable model-variant for a region (UX/infra ticket created).
- Document step-by-step: "If p99 > 800ms and KV cache hit < 60% -> route to fallback variant -> run cache-warm job". Add to hosted-api runbook (owner: Marcus).

Action items (short):
- Marcus Li — pin qv2 rollback for us-west1 and add rollback checklist (done 2026-06-18 04:00 UTC).
- Sofia Gomez — add synthetic small-chat load tests & expose per-variant cache metrics (in-progress, due 2026-06-25).
- Jordan Reed — fix retry idempotency tests + release consumer fix (in review, due 2026-06-30).
- Monitoring team — threshold tweak proposal for p99 alert; add consumer-group rebalance alert (todo, due 2026-06-22).

Unresolved / questions to investigate:
- Why did the kernel upgrade correlate with increased collectives latency only under partial (not full) load? Kernel / driver telemetry correlation needed.
- Are there prompt templates in the wild that cause extreme batch fragmentation? Need a small corpus analysis (product/solutions to provide examples).

Handoff notes for next on-call (to: Priya Kaur):
- All immediate mitigations are in place. qv2 is pinned in us-west1; embed consumer hotfix merged to main and should be deployed to staging first.
- Watch p99 for hosted-api, and KV cache hit-rate for model_variant=qv2 and fallback variants.
- If p99 climbs > 800ms for > 10m, revert runtime-routing to baseline and notify infra lead.

Misc / notes-to-self:
- Add a small script that snapshots model_variant cache metrics every 5m during rollouts and posts to a short-lived dashboard.
- Consider adding a short pre-rollout checklist for quantized variants: tokenization diff test + cache-warm smoke test + quick synthetic small-chat pass.

Next steps: schedule a 60-min deep dive with applied-ml + infra + runtime next week (invite tentative: 2026-06-22 16:00 UTC) to: 1) confirm tokenization issue, 2) plan durable fix for batching heuristics, 3) agree on monitoring improvements.

Raw links used during triage:
- live metrics: https://metrics.redwood.ai/d/hosted-api/latency?from=now-1h
- logs sample (INC-2387): https://logs.redwood.ai/query?cursor=inc2387-343
- hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/412

End of diary entry.
